note: Everything that did not behave as documented, including defects in our own earlier outputs.

items.finding: dist_visible_fault, visible_fault_dens_5k and visible_fault_dens_20k are computed
from the visible catalogue and are exactly zero (or maximal) on the catalogue
pixels that form the training presence set. A model that sees them separates the
training data (train loss ~0.02, i.e. near-perfect) and then scores AUC 0.500 on
withheld segments. Removing them lifts the holdout AUC from 0.500 to 0.8354.
items.handling: All three are excluded from every model in this repository and from the released
candidate. Recorded in scripts/build_candidate.py (LEAKY) and on the
hypotheses and research pages.

items.finding: Clamping the effort channels to a common 'fully mapped' reference
(dist_lidar -> 0, mapscale_field -> 2.0, trace_density and therm_dens_all -> p95)
puts the model on an out-of-distribution design. The resulting counterfactual
field came out ANTI-correlated with the withheld faults (AUC 0.0122, i.e. 0.988
in the wrong direction), and the derived gap field lambda_new inherited it
items.handling: The arm is retained in src/gems59/intensity.py and reported as a NEGATIVE
result. The released field does not use the counterfactual gap.

items.finding: A quadrant-blocked holdout removes every catalogue pixel from a whole quarter of
the map, so the catalogue-derived channels have nothing to refer to inside the
held-out block: dist_visible_fault scores AUC 0.509 there. That is not the
deployment condition, where the whole catalogue is known and the question is what
is missing from it.
items.handling: The instrument was extended with a segment-level fold
(holdout.assign_blocks_random) that withholds whole 8-connected catalogue
components while leaving the rest of the catalogue visible everywhere. Both
fold families exist; the release is measured with the segment-level one, which
matches deployment.

items.finding: The literal drift rule 'more than 70% of your dots within 3 px of one registry
raster's dots' is triggered by 20 of the 696 registered rasters, but those are
dense continuous surfaces: several are positive over all 5,167,373 footprint
pixels, so ANY dot pattern lands within 3 px of them. Applied literally the rule
cannot be satisfied by any candidate.
items.handling: The gate now also reports the chance-corrected lift = observed overlap / share
of the footprint within 3 px of that raster's dots. Among the 20 literal
offenders the maximum lift is 1.068 (on a 272,853-dot raster); the global
maximum lift is 1.999 on a 244-dot raster whose raw overlap is 0.0012. Both are
reported verbatim in evidence/uniqueness_dots.json rather than resolved by
picking the convenient number.

items.finding: The first implementation of the emitter ran one maximum_filter pass per integer
window size up to the maximum spacing, so a constant spacing map of 6 px cost six
full-grid passes. Separately, the non-maximum window and the inhibition radius
were coupled, which capped the achievable dot count at ~29k.
items.handling: One pass per distinct requested window size, and an explicit nms_half that
decouples the pre-filter window from the inhibition radius. Verified: minimum
pairwise separation of the released dots is 3.162 px over a 3,000-dot sample.

items.finding: A raster carrying NaN outside the bounds satisfies the rules but is rejected by
the portal with 'Predicted values must be in range [0, 1]', because the range
check reads the whole array. This is the error the owner hit.
items.handling: The release writes 0.0 outside the footprint. A -nan twin is still produced for
research and is NOT the advertised download. The writer re-reads and re-validates
its own output; all 12 checks pass on the released bytes.

items.finding: A Poisson-loss gradient-boosting fit with quadrature exposure weights produced an
almost flat intensity (peak only 9% above the mean) at 60 boosting iterations, so
the break-even bar was either cleared by 4.5 M pixels or by none.
items.handling: Switched to the case-control logistic discriminant converted with the odds
(Prentice & Pyke 1979), which is far better conditioned at this class imbalance.
Documented as an approximation to the IPP, not the exact IPP estimate, per
Fithian & Hastie 2013.

items.finding: The competition bytes cannot be fetched from drivendata.org without a login. They
are restored here from owner-supplied public GitHub mirrors.
items.handling: Every file is verified against the sha256 pinned in registry/data_manifest.json
before use, and the receipt is written to data/restore_receipt.json. A matching
digest proves transport identity, NOT organizer-authenticated origin; this is
stated on the sources page and in the README.
